lander_tower.label: Lander power tower
lander_tower.provenance: [ASSUMPTION] shared surface power station (K8 PSR tower) serving N rovers; reuses the [CALIB] recharge power, not a new fabricated value.

surface_pad.label: Surface charge pad
surface_pad.provenance: [CALIB] no published IPEx solar/charge spec; matches ipex_specs.RECHARGE_POWER_W (700 W).

lander_tower.label: Surface power tower / lander
lander_tower.provenance: [ASSUMPTION] a shared surface power station (K8 PSR tower) that can serve N vehicles; continuous_w reuses the [CALIB] recharge power, not a new fabricated value.

sinter.label: Sinter head (regolith fuser)
sinter.provenance: [CALIB] energy = constants.SINTER_ENERGY_J_PER_KG (thermodynamic floor); product density = constants.RHO_SINTERED (microwave-sinter measured). Its host platform's mass/power are not sourced -> kept as a tool, not a fabricated vehicle.

ez_rassor.label: EZ-RASSOR-geometry rover (render body)
ez_rassor.provenance: Geometry = the MIT EZ-RASSOR URDF (FlaSpaceInst/UCF; docs/ezrassor_assets.md), the body the default Godot mesh + the rover.py globals describe. Energy/drum REUSE the IPEx-grounded model -- EZ-RASSOR's own mass/power are not separately sourced and are NOT fabricated here. Mirrors rover.WHEEL_GAUGE_M/WHEEL_BASE_M/WHEEL_RADIUS_M + CG_HEIGHT_M.

ipex.label: ISRU Pilot Excavator (IPEx)
ipex.provenance: ipex_specs.py (Schuler et al., IPEx TRL-5, NTRS 20240008162); a RASSOR-lineage drum excavator -> no sinter tool on the baseline platform. Geometry: wheel r + drum sourced; track = 0.7 x RASSOR-2 0.5207 m; wheelbase/CG [CALIB]. Render body = CC0 self-authored (scripts/gen_ipex_mesh.py).

rassor2.label: RASSOR 2.0 (TRL-4 breadboard precursor)
rassor2.provenance: RASSOR 2.0 breadboard (Mueller 2016 / Schuler 2022 BD-scaling): dry mass 65 kg, large bucket drum 24.98 kg/drum x2, 43 cm wheels (r 0.215), 0.5207 m skid-steer track -- all SOURCED. wheelbase/CG [CALIB]. Energy reuses the IPEx model (RASSOR-2's own power not separately sourced; not fabricated). The TRL-4 precursor, registered so vehicle selection drives the planner numbers (its bigger per-cycle drum -> fewer drum cycles than IPEx).
